ci_serving_burst.note: capacity / vLLM-nightly parity evidence only; not the headline decode t/s/u

named_limitations: Warmed single-user decode cannot be improved from the serving layer: it already sits on the model's own traced token-out decode (23.155 ms/token served against a 23.1647 ms/token generator floor measured without vLLM, with the allocation caveat in README section 1). The remaining gap to the 1.111 ms/token roofline is the decoder stack's, measured and named by doc/optimized_full_model/ and doc/datatype_sweep/.

A request at a prompt length no earlier request used still compiles 3-13 programs and pays one decode-trace re-capture: 1.03-2.25 s when tt-metal must build those kernels, 0.03-0.10 s when it can load them, plus a ~230 ms stall on the first decode step. This is the LARGEST residual class - the 56-program re-capture bucket on a 32-slot server is 8 new logical lengths x 7 programs, not a slot remap. It is NOT closed off by an op contract: an earlier claim that ttnn.slice has no tensor-valued form was refuted in review round 3 from slice_nanobind.cpp/slice.cpp/slice_device_operation.cpp, which do expose a runtime-bounds overload. That overload takes an even split of slice_dim into num_devices parts and still wants a TILE output tile-aligned, so the adapted form is the 32-row window containing the last token plus a within-tile selection - a named, unverified candidate. README section 3.3 A.

Two further compile classes survive the warm-up, both measured and both with a written-then-reverted fix: a multi-chunk prompt compiles 6 programs per new chunk offset (candidates/prefill_chunk_offsets.json - the 19-program bucket is 2 new offsets plus one new tail length, not 4 offsets) and a slot remap compiles about 2 programs per row index not moved before (candidates/slot_program_keys.json plus the log ordering: 4/4/8 at widths 2/4/8, 20 at width 10, 64 at a first width-32 remap on both trees). Prefilling into a slot compiles nothing, so multi-request prefill is not a class. README section 3.3 B and C.

A single user on a --max-num-seqs 32 server pays the 32-row decode step (138.1 ms/token against 23.2 at --max-num-seqs 1). Measured to be per-row DeltaNet/attention work, not idle-row expert routing: before/batch_occupancy.json and batch_occupancy_distinct.json show 137.96 ms/token at 1 active row and 143.23 at 32, with and without a shared routed-expert union. Removing it needs batch-bucketed decode traces, which the recurrent state's per-pack layout blocks - README section 6 limitation 4.

The cold-JIT-cache arm of the new-length measurement was completed for the before tree only; the two launches attempted for the after arm were OOM-killed by the host kernel, as were three more after them (README section 7; 13 launch attempts in total, 8 of which came up). The after tree's cold-JIT first-request cost is composed from the same run's already-built-block rows (1.03-2.25 s) and labelled as composed.
No device-profiler, Tracy or tt-perf-report evidence was collected in this stage, by instruction; no watcher run either, because this stage changed no kernel, memory config, CCL or captured graph.

after_cold_jit_cache_reduced_two_layer_t.caveat: cache state not controlled for that run; quoted as an observation, not as the cold-cache cost

warmup_programs.before: not counted on that tree; program cache held 402 entries (max_num_seqs=1) / 448 (32) when warm-up finished

cold_kernel_cache_bound.basis: this stage's own cold-JIT before server built the same 402-entry program set in 73.74 s (07:12:33.615 -> 07:13:47.354) where the warm before server took 2.255 s (06:47:10.152 -> 06:47:12.407)
cold_kernel_cache_bound.note: paid once per machine - the tt-metal kernel cache is on disk - and on a cold machine it is mostly a relocation of build time that would otherwise land inside user requests. A deployment that only ever uses two or three block shapes does build more total kernels than before; ORNITH_VLLM_PREFILL_WARMUP takes an explicit list for that case.
